name_zh: 稀疏加速度的事件保留修复
formal_object: A full coordinate trajectory y; anchored free coordinates z; second time-difference D2 with actual timestep units; positive observation metric M.

operations.condition: Timestamps and time units are retained

operations.output: Dual balls preserve sparse dynamic events

operations.input: Quadratic data fit plus acceleration sparsity
operations.condition: Positive definite observation metric and exact anchor constraints

derivation_steps.statement: Solve min_y .5||y-yhat||_M^2 + lambda sum_(t,v)||D2 y||_2, with A y=X.
derivation_steps.justification: This encodes piecewise velocity rather than uniformly small acceleration.
Cauchy-Schwarz gives equality with p along a.

derivation_steps.statement: Write y=y_p+S z, A y_p=X, A S=0. Stationarity is S^T M(y_p+S z-yhat)+(D2 S)^T p=0.
derivation_steps.justification: Retain anchor and off-diagonal metric terms; if M_free=S^T M S, the effective center is M_free^-1 S^T M(yhat-y_p), not automatically the free entries of yhat.

assumptions: Real motion need not be piecewise velocity; sinusoidal or rapidly articulated motion can be biased.
Groups are 3D vectors, avoiding an arbitrary axis-wise L1 convention.
Tuning and timestamp scaling are frozen before confirmation.
Acceleration sparsity is an inference prior, not a new benchmark metric or event label.
method_expression: Apply anchored group trend filtering to native coordinates with the same original timestamps; preserve all motion events the optimizer retains.
distinguishing_prediction: Sparse abrupt changes should survive better than equal-strength Gaussian smoothing; smooth high-frequency real motion can be a failure boundary.
falsifier: Reject if Gaussian/second-order quadratic smoothing at equal tuning/compute matches official CD-M and geometry, or if event-like true motion is suppressed.
closest_alternative: Classical trend filtering and STAC Gaussian temporal smoothing.
decisive_comparison: Base, confidence-weighted Gaussian smoothing, quadratic acceleration repair and group-trend repair; native scoring only, matched development tuning.
operational_delta: Changes the temporal regularity prior and dual constraint, not the Gaussian bandwidth; existing trend filtering is attributed.
feasibility_and_cost: Banded temporal optimization per coordinate group; likely cheaper than re-generation, but full mesh/scoring time is unmeasured.
structural_signature: Nonsmooth group acceleration sparsity rather than quadratic smoothing or low-rank estimation.
algebra_review_basis: Verified norm conjugacy, affine anchor handling and dimensional time scaling. No promise of correct event recovery.
empirical_status: Not implemented in this round; no native method comparison or outcome.
originality_status: Unadjudicated. Classical tools and historical related code are explicitly attributed.
